# Object events

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/storage/events

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/storage/events.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Every committed object change records a durable, versioned event in the project database. CubiBase Functions can subscribe to these events through storage triggers.

## The event contract

Three event types are defined: `storage.object.created`, `storage.object.updated`, and `storage.object.deleted`. Each event is schemaVersion 1 and carries identity and metadata — never file contents or credentials.

**storage.object.created**

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "eventId": "3f7a…",
  "eventType": "storage.object.created",
  "projectId": "4c8d…",
  "bucketId": "a11b…",
  "objectId": "9b1e…",
  "path": "images/mika.png",
  "sizeBytes": 182344,
  "mimeType": "image/png",
  "actorId": "user_mika",
  "source": "storage-api",
  "correlationId": "f2c6…",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-20T10:05:00.000Z"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `eventId` | Unique id; consumers deduplicate on it |
| `projectId` / `bucketId` / `objectId` | The exact identities involved |
| `path` / `sizeBytes` / `mimeType` | Logical path and verified metadata |
| `actorId` / `source` | Who made the change: user id or null; `storage-api`, `console`, `edge-function`, or `system` |
| `correlationId` | Ties the event to the upload session or request |
| `timestamp` | ISO-8601 commit time |

## Durability and delivery

- Events are written to a transactional outbox in the same database transaction as the catalog change — an event exists if and only if the change committed.
- A failed or expired upload never emits a creation event.
- Delivery is at-least-once with retries and exponential backoff; exhausted retries land in a queryable dead-letter state, never silently discarded.
- Consumers must be idempotent on `eventId`. The schema is versioned so future fields (causation, invocation depth) can be added without breaking consumers.

## Processing events with CubiBase Functions

CubiBase Functions subscribe to these events through storage triggers configured in the Console — pick a bucket, the event types (created, updated, deleted), and an optional key prefix. The event is delivered asynchronously after the storage operation commits, with at-least-once semantics, retries, and dead-letter handling. The handler contract and a working example are on the Storage event functions page.

Functions read source objects and write derived objects through the scoped CubiBase Storage API with a short-lived, single-invocation credential. Function-created objects count toward the same project and account quotas through the same service, and processing traffic is distinguished from external delivery without creating an accounting bypass. Recursion is bounded by invocation-depth tracking: events caused by a function carry `causationId` and a depth counter, and chained function-triggered executions stop at a fixed maximum depth.

Typical scenarios: generate image thumbnails on upload, process PDFs into derived files or application data, and run scheduled cleanup of expired files — all through the same authorization and quota machinery as any other client. The Image Processing and Scheduled Cleanup templates start from working code.

> **note**: The `source` field keeps the wire value `edge-function` for events caused by function executions — it is a stable enum from the original event contract, not a claim of globally distributed edge execution. CubiBase Functions run in a regional managed runtime.

## Additional resources

- [Storage overview](https://cubibase.com/docs/storage) The API surface today.
- [Storage event functions](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/storage-events) Handlers for object events.
- [Storage feature page](https://cubibase.com/features/storage) The product-level story.

title: Functions overview
text:
# Functions overview

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

TypeScript and JavaScript functions that run in an isolated managed runtime — never inside the CubiBase engine. Four trigger types, one execution pipeline, one set of quotas and logs.

## What CubiBase Functions are

A CubiBase Function is your code, deployed as an immutable version to a managed Node.js 22 runtime (AWS Lambda in production; an isolated child process in local development). The engine manages deployments, triggers, secrets and metering, but never executes your code in its own process.

> **Not SQL Functions**: PostgreSQL SQL/PLpgSQL functions run inside your project database and are managed under Database → SQL Functions. CubiBase Functions are separate: TypeScript/JavaScript in the managed runtime, managed under Functions. Database Event Triggers connect the two worlds — they invoke a CubiBase Function after a committed database change.

| Trigger | When it runs | Delivery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP | A request hits https://{slug}.api.cubibase.com/functions/{name} | Synchronous request/response |
| Database | After an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE commits on a subscribed table | Async, at-least-once, retried |
| Storage | After an object is created, updated or deleted in a subscribed bucket | Async, at-least-once, retried |
| Scheduled | A cron expression fires (UTC or a configured timezone) | Async, at-least-once, retried |

All four categories produce the same invocation envelope and pass through the same authorization, quota reservation, concurrency control, metering and logging. There is no per-trigger side channel that skips enforcement.

## The programming model

Default-export an async handler `(request, ctx)`. Return a web `Response`, a `{ status, headers, body }` object, a plain object (serialized as JSON), a string, or nothing (204).

**index.ts**

```text
// index.ts — default-export an async (request, ctx) handler.
export default async function handler(request: any, ctx: any) {
  const name = request.query.name ?? 'world';
  console.log('Saying hello to', name);
  return new Response(JSON.stringify({
    message: `Hello, ${name}!`,
    invocationId: ctx.invocationId,
  }), { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } });
}
```

| On `request` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `method`, `url`, `headers`, `query` | The HTTP request as received by the gateway |
| `body` | A Buffer with the EXACT raw request bytes (HTTP triggers) — safe for signature verification |
| `json()` / `text()` | Parse helpers over the raw body |
| `event` | The structured payload for database, storage and scheduled triggers |
| `trigger` | `http`, `database`, `storage`, `schedule` or `test` |
| `auth` | The verified caller context (kind and user id, when authenticated) |
| `invocationId`, `correlationId` | Identifiers that appear in Executions & Logs |

| On `ctx` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.db.from(table)` | Scoped select / insert / update / delete with equality filters, through the project’s own roles and policies. JWT-authenticated HTTP calls run under the caller’s row-level security; trusted database, storage and scheduled invocations run with the project’s developer-level access |
| `ctx.db.query(sql, params)` | Read-only parameterized SQL through the project’s SQL role |
| `ctx.storage.from(bucket)` | upload, download, getMetadata, remove, list — through the same Storage quotas and events |
| `ctx.env` | Your environment variables and secrets for this deployment (frozen snapshot) |
| `ctx.log`, `console.*` | Captured into the bounded, redacted execution log |
| `ctx.waitUntil(promise)` | Background work with at most 5 extra seconds after the response |

> **note**: The runtime holds no AWS credentials, no database passwords and no other project’s data. The only platform credential is a token scoped to this single invocation, valid for minutes. Database and storage access goes through scoped CubiBase service APIs.

## Deployments and versions

- Editing source in the Console changes the working copy only. Deploy builds and publishes an immutable version.
- Bundling uses esbuild to transform your code — build scripts are never executed and no per-deploy npm install runs.
- Imports are limited to Node built-ins and a pinned dependency allowlist (currently the official Stripe SDK). Other imports fail the build with a clear error.
- Artifacts are stored in a private S3 bucket; the database keeps only references and checksums.
- A successful deploy atomically switches the active pointer. A failed deploy never interrupts the version that is serving.
- Activate any earlier ready version to roll back.

## In the Console

Open a project and choose Functions. My Functions lists every function with its triggers, deployment state and error rate. The editor has tabs for Source, Triggers, Security & Config, Secrets & Env, Deployments, Test and Logs. Executions & Logs shows every invocation across all trigger types; Usage & Quotas shows consumption against your plan.

- [HTTP functions](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/http) Endpoints, auth modes and calling conventions.
- [Database events](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/database-events) After-commit triggers with an outbox.
- [Storage events](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/storage-events) React to object lifecycle changes.
- [Scheduled functions](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/schedules) Cron without a scheduler of your own.

## Additional resources

- [Functions feature page](https://cubibase.com/features/functions) The product-level story.
- [Templates](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/templates) Eight working starting points.
- [Quotas and metering](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/quotas) What is counted and what happens at a limit.

title: HTTP functions
text:
# HTTP functions

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/http

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/http.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Every deployed function with an HTTP trigger is an HTTPS endpoint at https://{slug}.api.cubibase.com/functions/{name}. The gateway enforces authentication, signatures and limits before your code runs.

## The endpoint

GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS are supported. Headers, query parameters, extra path segments and the raw body reach your handler unchanged. The response your handler returns is the response the caller receives (bounded by the platform response-size limit).

**Call a public function**

```http
curl "https://example-project.api.cubibase.com/functions/hello-world?name=Ada"

# {"message":"Hello, Ada!","invocationId":"…"}
```

> **note**: The raw body is preserved byte-for-byte. Never re-serialize a parsed body before verifying a webhook signature — verify against request.body.

## Authentication modes

Authentication is a gateway setting, independent of your code and of payload signatures. JWT is the default when you create a function.

| Mode | Caller must present | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jwt` (default) | Authorization: Bearer <end-user access JWT> from CubiBase Auth | Calls from your signed-in users |
| `public` | Nothing | Webhooks and open endpoints — pair with signature verification |
| `api_key` | A project secret API key (cb_sec_…) in the apikey header or as Bearer | Server-to-server calls from trusted code |
| `internal` | Not externally reachable at all | Functions invoked only by other CubiBase machinery |

**JWT mode · call as a signed-in user**

```http
curl -X POST "https://example-project.api.cubibase.com/functions/openai-proxy" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <USER_ACCESS_JWT>" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "Summarize row-level security in one sentence."}'
```

**API key mode · call from your server**

```http
curl -X POST "https://example-project.api.cubibase.com/functions/send-email" \
  -H "apikey: cb_sec_YOUR_SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"to": "ada@example.com", "subject": "Welcome", "text": "Glad you are here."}'
```

> **Secret keys stay server-side**: API-key mode requires the secret key (cb_sec_…), not the publishable key. Never ship a secret key in a browser or mobile bundle. An internal-mode function answers 404 on the public host.

## Gateway responses

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | Missing/invalid JWT, missing/invalid secret key, or a failed signature check |
| `404` | Unknown project host, unknown function, no enabled HTTP trigger, or internal-only function |
| `409` | The function is disabled, or has no active deployment yet |
| `413` | The request body exceeds the platform request-size limit |
| `402` | The monthly invocation or compute allowance is exhausted |
| `429` | The per-project HTTP rate limit or concurrent-execution limit is reached — retry shortly |
| `500` | The function threw or exceeded its configured timeout (status recorded as timeout) — details are in Executions & Logs, not in the caller response |
| `502` | The function returned an oversized response |

Internal errors never leak infrastructure details to the caller. The invocation id in the error body matches the execution record in the Console.

## Additional resources

- [Signed payloads](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/signatures) HMAC verification and third-party webhooks.
- [Templates](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/templates) Stripe and GitHub webhook starting points.

title: Signed payloads and webhooks
text:
# Signed payloads and webhooks

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/signatures

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/signatures.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Payload signature verification is independent of caller authentication. Use built-in CubiBase HMAC-SHA256 for your own senders, or verify a provider’s scheme (Stripe, GitHub) inside your function against the exact raw body.

## Three signature settings

| Setting | Verified by | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | Nobody — authentication mode still applies | JWT/API-key protected endpoints |
| `hmac` | The gateway, before your code runs | Your own servers and services sending webhooks |
| `custom` | Your function code, using request.body and request.headers | Stripe, GitHub and other providers with their own schemes |

> **important**: A JWT or API key proves who called — not that the payload is intact. For public webhook endpoints, always require a signature: built-in HMAC for your senders, provider-specific verification for third parties.

## Built-in HMAC-SHA256

When HMAC mode is enabled, the gateway rejects any request without a valid signature. The signed input is `timestamp + "." + nonce + "." + rawBody`, HMAC-SHA256 with the function’s signing secret, hex-encoded.

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `x-cubibase-timestamp` | Unix seconds; must be within the tolerance window (default 300 s) |
| `x-cubibase-nonce` | 16–128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9._-], single use per function |
| `x-cubibase-signature` | hex(HMAC_SHA256(secret, `${timestamp}.${nonce}.${rawBody}`)) |

**Sign a delivery from your server**

```ts
import { createHmac, randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';

const body = JSON.stringify({ order: 4711, total: 4200 });
const timestamp = String(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000));
const nonce = randomBytes(16).toString('hex'); // 16–128 chars, single use
const signature = createHmac('sha256', process.env.CUBIBASE_SIGNING_SECRET)
  .update(`${timestamp}.${nonce}.`)
  .update(body) // EXACT raw bytes you send — never re-serialize
  .digest('hex');

await fetch('https://example-project.api.cubibase.com/functions/orders-hook', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'content-type': 'application/json',
    'x-cubibase-timestamp': timestamp,
    'x-cubibase-nonce': nonce,
    'x-cubibase-signature': signature,
  },
  body,
});
```

- Comparison is constant-time; the timestamp must be fresh; each nonce can be used once — replays are rejected with 401 signature_replayed.
- The signing secret is shown once when you enable HMAC or rotate it, and stored encrypted. It is never returned by read APIs and never logged.
- Rotation keeps the previous secret valid, so senders can roll over without dropped deliveries.

## Stripe, GitHub and other providers

Third parties cannot satisfy a CubiBase-specific format, and the platform does not force one on them. Set authentication to public and signature mode to custom, then verify the provider’s own header inside your handler using request.body (the exact raw bytes) and request.headers.

- Stripe: verify Stripe-Signature (t=timestamp, v1=HMAC) with your whsec_… signing secret, stored as STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The Stripe Webhook template does this with the official SDK and handles event idempotency.
- GitHub: verify X-Hub-Signature-256 (sha256=HMAC of the raw body) with the secret you configured on the hook. The GitHub Webhook template is ready to edit.
- Reject invalid signatures with a 4xx before any side effects. Return a fast 2xx only after the work (or its durable record) succeeded.

## Additional resources

- [Templates](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/templates) The Stripe and GitHub handlers, ready to deploy.
- [Secrets](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/secrets) Where signing secrets live.

# Database event functions

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/database-events

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/database-events.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Run a CubiBase Function after an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE commits on a table you choose. Events are captured atomically with your data change and delivered asynchronously — a function failure can never roll back your transaction.

## Configure a trigger

In the function editor open Triggers → Add trigger → Database events. Pick the table (public schema in the current release) and the operations; optionally include the previous record for UPDATE/DELETE. The platform installs a generated PostgreSQL trigger that writes to a transactional outbox (`functions.events_outbox`) in your project database — you never write trigger SQL yourself.

**Trigger configuration**

```json
{
  "kind": "database",
  "config": {
    "schema": "public",
    "table": "orders",
    "events": ["INSERT", "UPDATE", "DELETE"],
    "includeOldRecord": true
  }
}
```

- One function can subscribe to several tables; one table can feed several functions.
- Schema and table identifiers are validated; the generated trigger SQL is injection-safe.
- Removing the subscription drops the installed PostgreSQL trigger.
- Events are captured only for committed transactions — a rolled-back write produces no event.

## The event payload

**request.event · database.insert**

```text
// request.event on a database trigger (schemaVersion 1)
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "eventId": "8c1f…",
  "type": "database.insert",
  "projectId": "4c8d…",
  "schema": "public",
  "table": "orders",
  "operation": "INSERT",
  "newRecord": { "id": "…", "total": 4200, "user_id": "…" },
  "oldRecord": null,
  "actorUserId": "user_ada",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-20T10:05:00.000Z",
  "correlationId": "…"
}
```

`oldRecord` is null unless you enabled “include previous record”. `actorUserId` carries the end-user id when the write came through the Data API with a user JWT.

## Delivery semantics

- At-least-once: a delivery can repeat after a retry. Deduplicate on eventId — the template shows the pattern.
- Retries use exponential backoff; exhausted deliveries land in a queryable dead-letter state (Executions & Logs → Delivery queue).
- Function writes go through the same scoped database access as any invocation; recursion depth is capped.
- Outbox rows are cleaned up on a retention schedule; inactive projects are not polled without bound.

**Idempotent change handler**

```ts
export default async function handler(request: any, ctx: any) {
  const event = request.event;
  // At-least-once delivery: skip work you already did for this eventId.
  const seen = await ctx.db.from('processed_events').select({ event_id: event.eventId });
  if (seen.rows?.length > 0) return { duplicate: true };

  const record = event.operation === 'DELETE' ? event.oldRecord : event.newRecord;
  await ctx.db.from('audit_log').insert([{
    table_name: event.table,
    operation: event.operation,
    event_id: event.eventId,
    record_id: String(record?.id ?? ''),
    occurred_at: event.timestamp,
  }]);
  await ctx.db.from('processed_events').insert([{ event_id: event.eventId }]);
  return { ok: true };
}
```

> **note**: This is not a synchronous constraint mechanism. If a rule must block the write itself, use a PostgreSQL constraint or a native database trigger (Database → Database Triggers). CubiBase Functions react after commit.

## Additional resources

- [Native database triggers](https://cubibase.com/docs/database/triggers) Synchronous SQL triggers, a different tool.
- [Templates](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/templates) Database Change Handler and Send Email.

title: Storage event functions
text:
# Storage event functions

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/storage-events

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/storage-events.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Run a CubiBase Function when an object is created, updated or deleted in a bucket you choose. Events come from the existing Storage event stream — only successfully completed operations emit them.

## Configure a trigger

In the function editor open Triggers → Add trigger → Storage events. Pick the bucket, the lifecycle events, and optionally an object-key prefix filter.

**Trigger configuration**

```json
{
  "kind": "storage",
  "config": {
    "bucket": "images",
    "events": ["storage.object.created"],
    "prefix": "uploads/"
  }
}
```

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `storage.object.created` | An upload was verified and finalized |
| `storage.object.updated` | An existing path was replaced (explicit overwrite) |
| `storage.object.deleted` | An object was deleted |

- A failed, abandoned or expired upload never emits an event.
- The payload carries bucket, object id, path, size, MIME type, actor and timestamp — never file contents.
- Read and write files through ctx.storage; every function write counts toward the same storage and bandwidth quotas and emits its own events.

## Process an upload

**Derivative writer**

```ts
export default async function handler(request: any, ctx: any) {
  const event = request.event; // storage.object.created, schemaVersion 1
  console.log('New object:', event.path, event.sizeBytes, 'bytes');

  const source = await ctx.storage.from(event.bucketName).download(event.path);
  // ...transform source.body (a Buffer) here...

  // Write derivatives to a DIFFERENT prefix so this function does not
  // re-trigger itself. Function writes count toward the same quotas.
  await ctx.storage.from(event.bucketName).upload(
    event.path.replace(/^uploads\//, 'processed/'),
    source.body,
    { mimeType: source.mimeType, overwrite: true },
  );
  return { processed: event.path };
}
```

> **Avoid trigger loops**: A function that writes into the same bucket and prefix it watches would re-trigger itself. Keep input and output prefixes separate (uploads/ → processed/). As a backstop, the platform tracks invocation depth and drops chains beyond the configured cap — but filtering is the correct fix.

## Delivery semantics

The same durable queue as database events: at-least-once delivery, dedupe on eventId, exponential-backoff retries, dead-letter state after exhaustion. The event contract is shared with the Storage events documentation.

## Additional resources

- [Storage event contract](https://cubibase.com/docs/storage/events) The schemaVersion 1 payload in full.
- [Templates](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/templates) Image Processing starts from this pattern.

text:
# Environment variables and secrets

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/secrets

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/secrets.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Per-function configuration in two classes: plain environment variables for non-sensitive values, and encrypted secrets for credentials. Both reach your code as ctx.env at invocation time.

## Variables vs secrets

|  | Environment variables | Secrets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visible in the Console | Yes, to project members | Names and timestamps only — never values |
| Storage | Function metadata | Encrypted at rest in the platform secrets store |
| Use for | Model names, sender addresses, feature flags | API keys, webhook signing secrets, tokens |
| In code | ctx.env.NAME | ctx.env.NAME (identical) |

- Names use uppercase letters, digits and underscores; a name cannot be both a variable and a secret.
- Platform-reserved prefixes (CUBIBASE_, AWS_) are rejected for your own values.
- Saving a secret again under the same name rotates it. Deleting one destroys the encrypted value.
- Values are snapshotted into each deployment. After changing configuration, redeploy so the active version picks it up — the Console tells you when this is needed.

## What never happens

- Secret values are never returned by read APIs, never included in deployment logs, and never sent to the browser after the initial save.
- Execution logs are redacted: authorization headers, bearer tokens, API keys and common credential patterns are masked before storage.
- One function cannot read another function’s secrets, and no function can read another project’s anything.
- The HMAC signing secret is separate from your named secrets, shown once at creation/rotation, with the previous secret kept valid during rollover.

> **warning**: Do not paste credentials into source code. Source is readable by every project member and is stored as the editable working copy. Use the Secrets tab.

## Additional resources

- [Signed payloads](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/signatures) Managing the HMAC signing secret.
- [Templates](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/templates) Each template lists its required secrets.

title: Function templates
text:
# Function templates

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/templates

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/templates.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Eight versioned starting points with working code, preselected triggers and security defaults, and step-by-step setup instructions. Everything they generate is editable.

## The catalog

| Template | Trigger | What it does | Required secrets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hello World | HTTP | JSON greeting; the smallest possible function | — |
| Stripe Webhook | HTTP (public, custom signature) | Verifies Stripe-Signature on the raw body; idempotent payment/subscription handling | STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY optional) |
| GitHub Webhook | HTTP (public, custom signature) | Verifies X-Hub-Signature-256 for push and issue events | GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET |
| Send Email | HTTP (API key) or Database | Transactional email through the Resend API | RESEND_API_KEY + EMAIL_FROM variable |
| OpenAI Proxy | HTTP (JWT) | Server-side OpenAI calls so your key never ships to browsers | OPENAI_API_KEY |
| Image Processing | Storage | Processes new uploads, writes derivatives to a separate prefix | — |
| Database Change Handler | Database | Audit logging for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, deduped on eventId | — |
| Scheduled Cleanup | Scheduled | Nightly removal of expired rows; edit to your schema | — |

In the Console, Functions → Templates shows the catalog with code previews. “Use template” preselects the trigger type, authentication mode, signature mode, timeout and memory, and walks you through the required secrets and external configuration.

## Stripe Webhook, end to end

1. **Create from the template** — The function is created with public authentication and custom signature mode — Stripe cannot send a CubiBase JWT, and no CubiBase HMAC is forced on it.
2. **Create the dedupe table** — CREATE TABLE stripe_events (id text PRIMARY KEY, type text, processed_at timestamptz); — the handler records every processed event id.
3. **Deploy and copy the URL** — The function URL is https://{slug}.api.cubibase.com/functions/{name}. Deploy first; the endpoint is live only after a successful deployment.
4. **Configure Stripe** — Stripe Dashboard → Developers → Webhooks → Add endpoint. Paste the URL; subscribe to payment_intent.succeeded and customer.subscription.deleted (or your events).
5. **Store the signing secret** — Copy the endpoint’s signing secret (whsec_…) into the STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET secret and redeploy. Optionally set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to use the official SDK verification path.
6. **Verify with a test event** — Send a test event from the Dashboard and check Executions & Logs. The integration is connected only when a signed test delivery succeeds — the Console never claims otherwise.

> **note**: The handler verifies the signature against the exact raw bytes, rejects invalid signatures with 400, skips already-processed event ids, and returns a fast 200 so Stripe does not retry unnecessarily.

## Additional resources

- [HTTP functions](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/http) Auth modes for webhook endpoints.
- [Secrets](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/secrets) Storing provider credentials safely.

title: Executions and logs

# Executions and logs

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/logs

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/logs.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Every invocation — HTTP, database, storage, scheduled and test — produces one execution record with timing, outcome and captured console output. Logs are bounded, redacted and isolated per project.

## What is recorded

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Invocation id / correlation id | Trace one run end to end; async events also carry their eventId |
| Trigger and deployment version | Which trigger fired and which immutable version ran |
| Status | success, error, timeout, rejected (quota), or running |
| Duration and billed duration | Wall time and the metered time (100 ms floor, rounded up to 100 ms, capped at the timeout) |
| Memory | Configured MB and peak RSS when available |
| HTTP status | For HTTP and test invocations |
| Error category and message | Redacted; infrastructure details never reach callers |

- console.log/info/warn/error are captured per execution: at most 200 lines, 4 KB per line, 64 KB total — the record flags truncation.
- Credentials are redacted before storage: authorization headers, bearer tokens, cb_sec_/cb_pub_ keys, JWTs, sk_live/sk_test and whsec_ patterns.
- Retention is plan-based (3 days Free, 14 Pro, 30 Business); older records are purged automatically.

## Finding a run

Functions → Executions & Logs lists executions with filters for function, trigger and status, plus pagination. Open a row for the full record and its log output. The Delivery queue view shows pending, retried and dead-lettered async events. Each function’s Logs tab shows the same data scoped to that function. There is no live streaming — refresh to see new runs.

## Additional resources

- [Quotas and metering](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/quotas) How durations become GB-seconds.

title: Function quotas and metering
text:
# Function quotas and metering

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/quotas

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/functions/quotas.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Functions use the same subscription and plan catalog as the rest of CubiBase. Limits are enforced by the engine on every trigger type — never only in the Console.

## What is limited

| Dimension | Scope | At the limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Functions per project | Project | Creating another function is refused (402) |
| Invocations | Organization (shared), per billing cycle | Invocations rejected (402); async events retry, then dead-letter |
| Compute (GB-seconds) | Organization (shared), per billing cycle | Same as invocations |
| Memory per function | Plan ceiling | Configuration above the ceiling is refused |
| Concurrent executions | Project | HTTP callers get 429; async events wait and retry |
| Deployment artifact size | Per deployment | The build fails; the active version keeps serving |
| Enabled schedules | Project | Creating another schedule is refused |
| Execution log retention | Plan | Older records are purged |

Monthly allowances are organization-level, shared across all projects, and follow the existing billing cycle: the Stripe period for paid plans, the calendar month (UTC) for Free — the same convention as storage bandwidth. Buying additional projects does not increase them. Counters are reserved atomically, so concurrent invocations cannot race past a limit.

## What is counted

- Every executed invocation counts — success, failure and timeout alike. Requests rejected by the gateway (auth, signature, quota, concurrency) never reach the runtime and are not billed as invocations.
- Compute is GB-seconds: configured memory (GB) × billed duration. Billed duration is the handler time rounded up to 100 ms increments, floored at 100 ms and capped at the configured timeout.
- All four trigger types and Console test invocations meter identically.

**Allowance exhausted**

```text
HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required

{
  "error": {
    "code": "FUNCTIONS_QUOTA_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "Monthly invocation allowance exhausted…",
    "details": { "quota": "functions_invocations_monthly", "limit": 100000, "used": 100000 }
  }
}
```

## Current plan values

> **Shared organization quotas**: Function invocations and compute are shared across all projects in your organization; buying additional projects does not increase them. Function count, concurrency and schedules are per project. The values below come from the published pricing catalog; the Console’s Usage page always shows the live values for your plan.

|  | Free | Pro | Business |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Functions per project | 5 | 25 | 100 |
| Invocations per month (shared) | 500,000 | 2,000,000 | 6,000,000 |
| Compute per month (shared) | 10,000 GB-s | 50,000 GB-s | 300,000 GB-s |
| Execution timeout | 5 sec | 30 sec | 60 sec |
| Max memory per function | 128 MB | 256 MB | 512 MB |
| Concurrent executions per project | 5 | 20 | 50 |
| Enabled schedules per project | 2 | 10 | 50 |
| Execution log retention | 3 days | 14 days | 30 days |

By default there are no automatic overage charges: a quota is a hard stop, not a bill. On Pro and Business you can opt in to additional usage (Console → Billing → Additional Usage): excess invocations and compute then bill at the published rates under a monthly spending limit you set — it is never enabled for you. Upgrading raises the limits immediately; the next cycle resets monthly counters. See the pricing page for the full plan comparison and rates, and the Console at Functions → Usage & Quotas for your live usage, warnings and exceeded state. Example host: example-project.api.cubibase.com.

## Additional resources

- [Pricing](https://cubibase.com/pricing) Plans and the full comparison table.
- [Platform quotas](https://cubibase.com/docs/platform/quotas) How quotas work across CubiBase.

# API routes

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/reference/routes

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/reference/routes.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Every public route on the project host, plus the control paths the Console uses. Your application calls the project host — not the control API.

## Data API

Base: `https://{slug}.api.cubibase.com`. Every route needs the `apikey` header and an end-user bearer token.

**Data API · /rest/v1**

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/rest/v1/{table}` | List rows with filters, select, order, limit, offset |
| `GET` | `/rest/v1/{table}/{id}` | Read one row by primary key |
| `POST` | `/rest/v1/{table}` | Insert one row · 201 |
| `PATCH` | `/rest/v1/{table}/{id}` | Update one row |
| `DELETE` | `/rest/v1/{table}/{id}` | Delete one row |
| `POST` | `/rest/v1/rpc/{function}` | Call a function granted to the api role · named JSON arguments |

## Auth API

Same host, under `/auth/v1`, with the same `apikey` header. Signup, sign-in, refresh, logout, and the Google flow do not need a bearer token; the user and factor routes do. A bearer token on authorize or the id_token grant links the Google identity to that user.

**Auth API · /auth/v1**

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/signup` | Create a user · 201 |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/signup/anonymous` | Create an anonymous session · 201 |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password` | Sign in (or an MFA challenge) |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/token?grant_type=refresh_token` | Refresh the session |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/token?grant_type=mfa` | Complete an MFA challenge |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/token?grant_type=id_token` | Verify a Google ID token |
| `GET` | `/auth/v1/authorize?provider=google` | Start the Google redirect flow |
| `GET` | `/auth/v1/callback` | Google redirects back here · 302 to your app |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/logout` | Revoke the session · 204 |
| `GET` | `/auth/v1/user` | Read the signed-in user |
| `PATCH` | `/auth/v1/user` | Update the user; convert anonymous users |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/factors` | Enroll a TOTP factor · 201 |
| `POST` | `/auth/v1/factors/verify` | Confirm the first TOTP code |
| `DELETE` | `/auth/v1/factors/{factorId}` | Remove a factor · 204 |

## Storage API

Same host, under `/storage/v1`, with the same `apikey` header. Writes and private reads need a bearer token (end-user JWT or secret API key); public-bucket reads need only the key. Every download is metered against the account’s monthly bandwidth.

**Storage API · /storage/v1**

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/storage/v1/buckets` | Create a bucket · 201 |
| `GET` | `/storage/v1/buckets` | List buckets |
| `GET` | `/storage/v1/buckets/{bucket}` | Bucket configuration |
| `PATCH` | `/storage/v1/buckets/{bucket}` | Update visibility, size cap, MIME allowlist |
| `DELETE` | `/storage/v1/buckets/{bucket}` | Delete the bucket and its objects |
| `POST` | `/storage/v1/objects/upload` | Start an upload · reserves quota, returns the S3 policy · 201 |
| `POST` | `/storage/v1/uploads/{id}/complete` | Verify and finalize the uploaded object |
| `GET` | `/storage/v1/uploads/{id}` | Upload session status |
| `GET` | `/storage/v1/objects` | List objects · bucket, prefix, delimiter, search, limit, offset |
| `GET` | `/storage/v1/objects/{id}` | Object metadata |
| `GET` | `/storage/v1/objects/{id}/content` | Download · metered, Range supported |
| `HEAD` | `/storage/v1/objects/{id}/content` | Download headers without bytes |
| `POST` | `/storage/v1/objects/{id}/sign` | Short-lived signed download link |
| `GET` | `/storage/v1/public/{bucket}/{path}` | Anonymous public-bucket read · metered |
| `DELETE` | `/storage/v1/objects/{id}` | Delete an object |
| `GET` | `/storage/v1/usage` | Project storage and bandwidth consumption |

## Functions API

Same host, under `/functions/{name}`. Authentication depends on the function’s configured mode: JWT bearer token (default), secret API key, public, or internal-only (404 externally). Payload signature headers are independent — see the Signed payloads docs page.

**Functions API · /functions**

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ALL` | `/functions/{name}` | Invoke a deployed HTTP function · GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS |
| `ALL` | `/functions/{name}/{path...}` | Extra path segments reach the handler unchanged |

## Control API paths (Console)

These are the paths the Console uses for accounts, projects, schema, rows, SQL, keys, the auth user directory, the Database menu managers (policies, SQL functions, triggers, indexes, types, views), storage, and CubiBase Functions management. They are listed for completeness; this guide does not publish a separate public base URL for them, and your application should not call them.

title: Error codes
text:
# Error codes

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/reference/errors

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/reference/errors.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

Every error is a JSON object with a stable code, a message, and a requestId. Match on the code, not the message text.

## The error shape

**Error response**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "missing_end_user_token",
    "message": "An end-user bearer token is required",
    "requestId": "req_example"
  }
}
```

Some errors add a `details` field (for example, which quota was exceeded). The `requestId` appears in the project’s request logs, so you can trace a failure from the Console.

## Authentication and sessions

| Status | Code | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | `missing_api_key` | Send the publishable key in the `apikey` header |
| `401` | `invalid_api_key` | The key is not active for this project; check or rotate it |
| `401` | `missing_end_user_token` | Send the user’s JWT as `Authorization: Bearer …` |
| `401` | `invalid_token` | Expired or unverifiable JWT; refresh the session |
| `401` | `session_revoked` | The session was revoked; sign in again |
| `401` | `mfa_required` | The project requires an MFA-verified session |
| `401` | `invalid_credentials` | Wrong email or password |
| `401` | `invalid_refresh_token` | Expired, revoked, or reused refresh token; sign in again |
| `401` | `invalid_challenge` | MFA challenge expired or already used |
| `401` | `invalid_mfa_code` | Wrong TOTP code |
| `401` | `invalid_id_token` | Google ID token failed verification or nonce check |
| `403` | `user_banned` | The user is banned in the Console |
| `403` | `signup_disabled` | Signup is switched off for the project |
| `403` | `password_signin_disabled` | Password sign-in is switched off |
| `403` | `anonymous_disabled` | Enable Allow anonymous sign-ins in Providers |
| `403` | `provider_disabled` | Enable Google sign-in in Providers |
| `403` | `mfa_disabled` | Enable MFA before enrolling factors |
| `403` | `mfa_enrollment_required` | Required MFA: the user must enroll a factor first |
| `400` | `weak_password` | Meet the minimum length; do not reuse the email |
| `400` | `conversion_requires_credentials` | Anonymous conversion needs email and password together |
| `400` | `unsupported_grant` | grant_type must be password, refresh_token, mfa, or id_token |
| `400` | `unsupported_provider` | Only the google provider is supported |
| `400` | `invalid_redirect` | redirect_to is not a valid http(s) URL |
| `400` | `redirect_not_allowed` | Add the URL to the App redirect allowlist |
| `400` | `invalid_state` | OAuth state missing, expired, or already used |
| `400` | `email_required` | The Google account did not provide an email |
| `409` | `user_exists` | A user with that email already exists |
| `409` | `identity_exists` | The Google account is linked to another user |
| `409` | `email_mismatch` | The Google email differs from the signed-in user’s |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | Too many attempts; back off and retry later |

## Data API

| Status | Code | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `invalid_filter` | Filters must be `column=op.value` with a supported operator |
| `400` | `invalid_column` | Unknown column, or a bad `select` list |
| `400` | `invalid_order` | order must be `column.asc` or `column.desc` (max 3) |
| `400` | `invalid_body` | Body must be a non-empty JSON object (max 64 fields); on RPC, named arguments that fit the parameters |
| `400` | `validation_error` | limit/offset out of range, or a bad row id |
| `400` | `not_null_violation` | A required column was omitted |
| `400` | `check_violation` | A value failed a check constraint |
| `400` | `invalid_input` | A value does not fit the column type |
| `400` | `numeric_overflow` | A number is out of range for the column |
| `403` | `forbidden` | The row policy rejected the read or write, or the api role lacks a table grant inside an RPC function |
| `404` | `not_found` | Unknown or unexposed table, a missing/hidden row, or an RPC function without a matching grant and arguments |
| `405` | `method_not_allowed` | Expose that operation on the table |
| `408` | `statement_timeout` | The query timed out; simplify it |
| `409` | `conflict` | Unique constraint violated |
| `409` | `foreign_key_violation` | The referenced row does not exist |
| `300` | `ambiguous_function` | Several RPC overloads match the arguments; details lists the signatures |
| `413` | `result_too_large` | An RPC set-returning function produced more than 10000 rows |

## Database objects (Console)

The Database menu managers — policies, functions, triggers, indexes, types, views — return these codes when a definition is rejected. Everything they manage lives in the public schema.

| Status | Code | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `validation_error` | A name, expression, or option failed validation; the details list the field |
| `400` | `invalid_definition` | PostgreSQL rejected the definition (e.g. a bad function body) |
| `400` | `invalid_column` | An expression or index references a column the table does not have |
| `400` | `invalid_sql` | The statement could not be executed as written |
| `400` | `undefined_function` | A trigger or expression references a function that does not exist |
| `400` | `not_supported` | The requested operation is not supported for that object |
| `403` | `extension_function` | The function belongs to an extension; it cannot be edited or dropped. Disable the extension instead |
| `404` | `not_found` | The object does not exist in the public schema |
| `409` | `already_exists` | An object with that name already exists |
| `409` | `object_in_use` | Other objects depend on it; drop the dependents first |

## Storage

The /storage/v1 endpoints return these codes. Quota errors include the limit and current consumption in details; private objects never leak their existence to unauthorized callers.

| Status | Code | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `402` | `STORAGE_PROJECT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | Project storage full; delete objects or upgrade |
| `402` | `STORAGE_ACCOUNT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | Account-wide storage full; delete objects or upgrade |
| `402` | `STORAGE_BANDWIDTH_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | Monthly download budget exhausted; resets next billing cycle |
| `413` | `STORAGE_FILE_TOO_LARGE` | File exceeds the plan or bucket maximum |
| `403` | `STORAGE_BUCKET_ACCESS_DENIED` | The caller cannot access this bucket |
| `410` | `STORAGE_UPLOAD_EXPIRED` | Upload session expired; start a new upload |
| `404` | `STORAGE_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` | Missing object, or private and not visible to you |
| `409` | `storage_object_exists` | Path already taken; pass overwrite: true to replace |
| `415` | `storage_mime_not_allowed` | MIME type not in the bucket allowlist |

## Functions

The /functions/{name} gateway returns these codes before or around execution. Quota and concurrency refusals never reach the runtime and are not metered as invocations. Execution failures (a thrown error or a timeout) return 500 with the invocation id; the details live in Executions & Logs, never in the caller response.

| Status | Code | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | `invalid_signature` | HMAC signature missing or wrong; sign the exact raw bytes you send |
| `401` | `signature_timestamp_expired` | Timestamp outside the tolerance window; use the current unix time |
| `401` | `signature_replayed` | The nonce was already used; generate a fresh nonce per delivery |
| `402` | `FUNCTIONS_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | Monthly invocations or GB-seconds exhausted; upgrade or wait for the cycle reset |
| `404` | `function_not_found` | Unknown function, no enabled HTTP trigger, or an internal-only function |
| `409` | `function_disabled` | The function is disabled; enable it in the Console |
| `409` | `function_not_deployed` | No active deployment yet; deploy the function first |
| `409` | `signature_not_configured` | HMAC mode is on but no signing secret exists; rotate the signature secret |
| `413` | `request_too_large` | Body exceeds the platform function request limit |
| `429` | `FUNCTIONS_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` | All concurrent execution slots are busy; retry shortly |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | Per-project HTTP rate limit reached; back off and retry |
| `502` | `response_too_large` | The handler returned an oversized response; return less data |
| `503` | `functions_disabled` | Functions is switched off on this engine deployment |

Management APIs (Console) additionally return `validation_error` for bad names, cron expressions or configurations, `name_conflict` when a secret and a variable share a name, `already_exists` for duplicate triggers, and `deployment_not_ready` when activating a version that is not ready.

## Project and platform

| Status | Code | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `402` | `quota_exceeded` | A shared quota (MAU, API requests, bandwidth, function invocations or compute) or a database-size limit was reached; `details` carries the resource, scope, usage, limit and reset date. Upgrade, reduce usage, or (paid plans) enable additional usage in Console → Billing → Additional Usage |
| `402` | `spending_limit_reached` | The organization enabled additional usage and its estimated metered spending reached the monthly spending limit; `details` carries the limit and current spend. Included quotas are unaffected. Raise the limit, reduce usage, or wait for the billing-period reset |
| `403` | `project_suspended` | Account over quota past the grace period; upgrade or reduce |
| `403` | `project_paused` | Free project idle 14 days; resume from the Console |
| `404` | `project_not_found` | Unknown slug, or the project is not active yet |
| `409` | `project_not_ready` | Provisioning has not finished |
| `400` | `invalid_sql` | The SQL editor accepts one read-only statement |
| `403` | `read_only` | The statement cannot modify data |
| `500` | `internal_error` | Unexpected failure; retry, and contact support with the requestId |

## Additional resources

- [API routes](https://cubibase.com/docs/reference/routes) Where each error can come from.
- [Quotas and suspension](https://cubibase.com/docs/platform/quotas) The 402 and 403 project states in detail.
- [Pause, archive, restore](https://cubibase.com/docs/platform/lifecycle) What project_paused means and how to clear it.

title: Using CubiBase with AI agents
text:
# Using CubiBase with AI agents

Source: https://cubibase.com/docs/agents

Also available: [Markdown version](https://cubibase.com/docs/agents.md) · [llms.txt](https://cubibase.com/llms.txt) · [full site content](https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt)

CubiBase is built to be operated by AI agents end to end: discover the API, authenticate with a personal access token, and act through an MCP server, a CLI, or plain HTTPS.

## The agent surfaces

| Surface | Where | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP server | `npx -y @cubibasehq/mcp` | Tools for chat and IDE agents (Claude, Cursor, Codex): projects, full schema, rows, SQL, storage uploads, function deployments, logs, Data API, docs search |
| CLI | `npx -y @cubibasehq/cli` | Shell agents and scripts; JSON output on stdout, structured errors on stderr. Same console parity as the MCP tools |
| TypeScript client | `npm install @cubibasehq/client` | Typed ControlClient and DataClient for code agents |
| Control API OpenAPI | `https://api.cubibase.com/v1/openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1 with operationIds and typed errors for the whole Control API |
| Data API OpenAPI | `https://{slug}.api.cubibase.com/rest/v1/openapi.json` | Per-project spec generated from the live schema: exposed tables, columns, filters, RPC functions |
| Skill file | `https://cubibase.com/SKILL.md` | A loadable skill (agentskills.io format) that teaches an agent the whole CubiBase workflow. Canonical repo: github.com/cubibase/skills; also inside the @cubibasehq/mcp and @cubibasehq/cli packages |

Source for all three packages: github.com/cubibase/cubibase-agent (MIT).

## Authentication an agent can finish

1. **Create a personal access token** — Console → Account → Access tokens. Scope read for inspection, write for building, admin for destructive operations. Optionally restrict the token to one project.
2. **Give the token to the agent** — Set CUBIBASE_TOKEN in the agent environment (MCP env block or shell). The token is a cb_pat_… string, shown once.
3. **Optional: add a service key for data access** — For Data API tools, create a secret key (cb_sec_…) in the project’s API keys and set CUBIBASE_SERVICE_KEY. It acts as the service actor; row-level security still applies.

> **important**: A service key is not a superuser. It runs with cubibase.role = 'service' and sees only rows that a service policy grants. Grant access explicitly, for example a SELECT policy using cubibase.current_role() = 'service'.

## MCP setup

Add the server to any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, and others):

**mcp.json**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cubibase": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@cubibasehq/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "CUBIBASE_TOKEN": "cb_pat_…",
        "CUBIBASE_SERVICE_KEY": "cb_sec_… (optional)"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

76 tools in seven groups. Projects: list, get, create, update, delete. Database: tables, columns, exposure, policies, PostgreSQL triggers, indexes, enum/composite types, views, rows (list/insert/update/delete), read-only SQL, SQL functions. Storage: bucket CRUD, object listing, cubibase_upload_file (end-to-end upload from text or base64), presigned upload URLs for large files, signed download links. Functions: create from source or template, deploy, activate deployments, secrets, http/database/storage/schedule triggers, test invocation, execution logs. Data API: cubibase_data_list, cubibase_data_rpc, cubibase_data_openapi. Observability: API keys, request logs, audit logs, usage, and cubibase_additional_usage (read-only V4.5 overage settings, per-resource excess and estimated costs, invoice preview — enabling overages stays a Console-only owner action). Docs: cubibase_search_docs searches the bundled documentation offline and returns excerpts with URLs.

| Environment variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `CUBIBASE_READ_ONLY=1` | Hides every mutating tool from the tool list. Pair with a read-scope token for safe exploration agents |
| `CUBIBASE_FEATURES=database,storage` | Only register the listed tool groups: projects, database, storage, functions, data, observability, docs |

**Read-only inspection server**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cubibase": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@cubibasehq/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "CUBIBASE_TOKEN": "cb_pat_…",
        "CUBIBASE_READ_ONLY": "1"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## CLI setup

**Shell**

```bash
export CUBIBASE_TOKEN=cb_pat_…
npx -y @cubibasehq/cli projects list
npx -y @cubibasehq/cli tables list <projectId>
npx -y @cubibasehq/cli rows list <projectId> notes --filter status=eq.active --limit 10
npx -y @cubibasehq/cli sql <projectId> 'select count(*) from notes'
npx -y @cubibasehq/cli storage upload <projectId> --bucket avatars --path u1.png --file ./u1.png
npx -y @cubibasehq/cli functions create <projectId> --name hello --file ./hello.ts
npx -y @cubibasehq/cli functions deploy <projectId> hello
```

Command groups: projects, tables, rows, sql, rpc, exposure, policies, triggers, indexes, types, views, storage, functions, keys, logs, usage, tokens. Every command prints JSON. Errors print {"error":{code,message,status,retryAfterSeconds}} to stderr and exit 1.

## Errors and retries

- Every error carries a stable machine code (e.g. invalid_token, insufficient_scope, quota_exceeded) and a requestId for support.
- 429 responses include a Retry-After header (seconds). Wait, then retry — do not hammer.
- 401 means re-authenticate or check the token scope; 403 means the action is not allowed for this actor; 402 means a plan quota was reached.
- The full error catalogue is on the error codes reference page.

## Machine-readable discovery files

- llms.txt — product summary and page index: https://cubibase.com/llms.txt
- llms-full.txt — the entire site content in one file: https://cubibase.com/llms-full.txt
- Markdown mirrors — every page is also served as {path}.md, e.g. https://cubibase.com/docs/quickstart.md
- Pricing as text: https://cubibase.com/pricing.md
- AI catalog: https://cubibase.com/.well-known/ai-catalog.json
- Skill file: https://cubibase.com/SKILL.md

## Additional resources

- [Personal access tokens](https://cubibase.com/docs/platform/access-tokens) Scopes, restrictions, rate limits, revocation.
- [API routes](https://cubibase.com/docs/reference/routes) Every Control and Data API route.
- [Error codes](https://cubibase.com/docs/reference/errors) The stable codes an agent can branch on.
